the estimation of the parameters of a model, in the presence of both uncertainty noise and outliers, and the estimation of the variance of the underlying Gaussian distribution.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we provide the following: (i) A theoretical study of the stability of the VoP of RANSAC estimators, which shows that there is a stable range of uncertainty bounds, (ii) An algorithm for computing this range, (iii) A new estimator, which is a combination of RANSAC and our algorithm.

we propose a new estimator for parameter estimation in presence both uncertainty and outliers, that is stable with respect to the variance of the noise, and that can be computed in a simple and efficient way.
The main takeaway from our work is that
stability can be used as a criterion to reject outliers in parameter estimation.
, in presence of uncertainty and outlier noise, the variance of a RANSAC estimate of a model parameter is stable with respect to the bound on the noise, and can be accurately computed.
, in the presence of uncertainty, stability of the solution is a necessary condition to obtain accurate parameter estimation and outlier rejection.
